methodTypes.name: ApiResourceReference
methodTypes.description:
Generic reference to any API resource by org and slug.
 Used across resources to reference other resources (e.g., Environment, Agent, Skill).
 Canonical format: "org/slug" (e.g., "stigmer/web-search", "acme/my-agent").

fields.name: Org
fields.description:
Organization that owns the referenced resource.

 When non-empty: must be a valid org slug (lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens,
 starts with a letter, 1-63 characters). Example: "stigmer", "acme-corp".

 When empty: the reference is relative — the server resolves it to the parent
 resource's organization at write time. All stored and returned references
 always have org populated (absolute form).

 Use empty org for same-org references (the common case).
 Use explicit org for cross-org references (e.g., marketplace resources).

fields.name: Kind
fields.description: Kind of the referenced resource (e.g., SKILL, AGENT, MCP_SERVER).

fields.name: Slug
fields.description:
Resource slug (user-friendly identifier, unique within org).
 Format: lowercase alphanumeric with hyphens, must start with a letter (e.g., "web-search", "code-reviewer").
 Length: 1-63 characters.

fields.name: Version
fields.description:
Version of the resource (optional, only applicable to versioned resources like Skills).
 Supports three formats:
 1. Empty/unset → Resolves to "latest" (most recent version)
 2. Tag name → Resolves to version with this tag (e.g., "stable", "v1.0")
 3. Exact hash → Immutable reference to specific version (e.g., "abc123...")

 Default behavior: Empty means "latest" (current version).
 This field is ignored for non-versioned resources.

 Examples:
 - version: ""           → Use latest version
 - version: "latest"     → Use latest version (explicit)
 - version: "stable"     → Use version tagged as "stable"
 - version: "v1.0"       → Use version tagged as "v1.0"
 - version: "abc123..."  → Use exact version with this hash (immutable)

enumTypes.name: ApiResourceVisibility
enumTypes.description:
Visibility controls who can access an API resource.
 This is orthogonal to ownership - visibility is about access control,
 while ownership (org) determines who manages the resource.

 Key distinction:
 - Ownership: Which organization controls/manages the resource
 - Visibility: Who can access/use the resource

 All resources belong to an organization. Visibility determines whether
 users outside that organization can access the resource.

values.name: visibility_private
values.description:
Only members of the owning organization can access.
 This is the default for most resources.
 Named visibility_private to avoid Java reserved keyword conflict.

values.name: visibility_public
values.description:
Anyone can access (read) this resource.
 Used for marketplace-published resources (e.g., "stigmer/web-search").
 Write access still requires org membership.
 Named visibility_public to avoid Java reserved keyword conflict.

resourceDescription:
Project groups related resources under a single unit of management with automatic orphan pruning.

 @internal
 Two tracks are supported:

 Declarative Track (no entry_point):
   Place YAML resource files alongside stigmer.yaml. The CLI scans the
   directory, applies each resource individually, and updates the project
   membership. Resources removed from the directory are pruned.

 SDK Track (entry_point set):
   The CLI executes the entry_point to synthesize resources, applies each
   individually, and updates the project membership. The runtime is inferred
   from the entry_point file extension (.go, .py, .ts, .js).

 In both tracks, the project stores only references (org/kind/slug) to its
 members — never full resource objects. Orphan pruning is a set-difference
 between previous and current members.

statusType.name: ProjectStatus
statusType.description:
ProjectStatus contains system-managed state for a Project.

 Minimal by design:
 - audit.updated_at tracks when the project was last applied
 - Member counts are derivable from spec.members (no duplication)
 - Errors are returned in Apply() response, not stored in status

fields.name: LastReconciliation
fields.description:
Reconciliation summary from the most recent Apply operation.
 Populated only in the Apply() response — not persisted to database.
 Reports orphan-pruned resources and any server-side changes.

fields.name: Audit
fields.description:
Standard audit information (created_at, updated_at, etc.)
 The updated_at field indicates when the project was last successfully applied.

statusNestedTypes.name: ReconciliationSummary
statusNestedTypes.description:
ReconciliationSummary contains the results of project reconciliation.
 Populated only in the ProjectCommandController.Apply() response to show
 what changes were made. NOT persisted to the database.

 In the reference-based model, individual resources are applied by the CLI
 before the project is applied. The server's reconciliation is limited to
 orphan pruning: comparing previous members with current members and
 deleting resources that are no longer in the membership list.

 All three fields use ApiResourceReference — the same type used in
 ProjectSpec.members — so reconciliation results are directly comparable
 with the membership list.

 Example CLI output:

	Applied project "my-app":
	  Members: 3 agents, 1 workflow, 2 mcp_servers
	  Pruned:  1 agent (removed from project)

fields.name: Created
fields.description: Resources created on the server during this project apply.

fields.name: Updated
fields.description: Resources updated on the server during this project apply.

fields.name: Deleted
fields.description:
Resources deleted via orphan pruning during this project apply.
 An orphan is a resource that was in the previous members list but
 is absent from the current members list.
